text: The applications concern the administrative arrest of the applicants prior to a demonstration.
The applications concern the detention of the applicants prior to a demonstration.
The applications concern the subsequent conviction of the applicants on charges of minor hooliganism.
The arrests and detention of the applicants occurred prior to a demonstration.
On 17 April 2011, the applicant in application no. 13509/12 (the first applicant) was a reporter at the time of his arrest.
On 17 April 2011, the first applicant was arrested before a demonstration of opposition to the government.
A record of the first applicant's administrative arrest was drawn up following his arrest on 17 April 2011.
An administrative-offence report was drawn up following the first applicant's arrest on 17 April 2011.

The administrative arrest record and administrative-offence report indicated that the first applicant had been arrested on 17 April 2011 for failure to comply with a lawful request of the police to stop swearing in the street.
The first applicant was charged with the administrative offence of minor hooliganism under Article 296 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.
The first applicant was kept in police custody overnight following his arrest on 17 April 2011.
On 18 April 2011, the first applicant was brought before the Sabail District Court.
The Sabail District Court found the first applicant guilty under Article 296 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.
The Sabail District Court sentenced the first applicant to a fine in the amount of 50 Azerbaijani manats (approximately 50 euros at the material time).
The domestic courts based their decision in the first applicant's case solely on the administrative-offence report.
The domestic courts based their decision in the first applicant's case solely on two witness statements from the police officers who had carried out his arrest.
The first applicant appealed against his administrative conviction.
In his appeal, the first applicant claimed that his arrest had been unlawful and unjustified.
In his appeal, the first applicant claimed that his detention had been unlawful and unjustified.
In his appeal, the first applicant claimed that the Sabail District Court's decision had not been sufficiently reasoned.
In his appeal, the first applicant claimed that he had not been provided with the administrative-offence report so that he could prepare his defence.
In his appeal, the first applicant claimed that he had not been provided with any other document so that he could prepare his defence.
By a final decision of 19 May 2011, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the first applicant's appeal as unsubstantiated.
The applicant in application no. 64801/12 (the second applicant) was the chairman of the Central Executive Office of the Musavat Party at the time of the events.
On 24 May 2012, opposition groups were planning to hold a demonstration.
The second applicant was planning to participate in the demonstration planned for 24 May 2012.
At 9.55 a.m. on 24 May 2012, the second applicant was walking with his grandson when he was stopped by two plainclothes police officers.
The two plainclothes police officers invited the second applicant to the police station at 9.55 a.m. on 24 May 2012.
The second applicant went with the police officers to the police station on 24 May 2012.
The second applicant was held at the police station for around seven hours on 24 May 2012.
The second applicant was asked various questions while held at the police station on 24 May 2012.
At 5 p.m. on 24 May 2012, the second applicant was brought before the Binagadi District Court.

The Binagadi District Court found the second applicant guilty of the administrative offence of failure to comply with a lawful request of a police officer under Article 310 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.
The Binagadi District Court sentenced the second applicant to a fine of 20 Azerbaijani manats (approximately 20 euros at the material time).
The second applicant appealed against his administrative conviction.
In his appeal, the second applicant claimed that he had been unlawfully deprived of his liberty.
In his appeal, the second applicant claimed that the Binagadi District Court had not given reasons for its decision.
In his appeal, the second applicant claimed that he had been arrested to prevent him from participating in the demonstration of 24 May 2012.
By a final decision of 21 June 2012, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the second applicant's appeal as unsubstantiated.
The applicants complained that their rights protected under Article 5 § 1 of the Convention had been breached by the domestic authorities.
The applicants complained that their rights protected under Article 6 § 1 of the Convention had been breached by the domestic authorities.
The applicants complained that their rights protected under Article 6 § 3 of the Convention had been breached by the domestic authorities.
The second applicant complained under Article 11 of the Convention of a violation of his right to freedom of assembly.
